THE METHOD BEHIND THE ESTIMATE

Under the hood.

Real held-out results from the project's model. R² is a score, not a percentage of correct prices.

02

A fair comparison

5-fold group CV

The model with the lowest cross-validation MAE is selected. Every model uses the same grouped splits.

ModelCV MAETest MAETest R²

Price errors are in TRY. Lower MAE is better; higher R² is better. These results describe the saved data split.

01

Prepare the data

Repeated rows are removed. Missing inputs are filled using training data only. Cars with identical basic details stay in the same split group.

02

Learn the patterns

CatBoost learns log prices using vehicle details. Five-fold cross-validation selects the model before the test set is evaluated.

03

Estimate in your browser

The trained decision trees and preprocessing are loaded here. Each estimate uses the exported model, with no separate prediction server.

A LITTLE CONTEXT GOES A LONG WAY

Know the limits.

Useful estimates start with understanding the data behind them.

What the number means

This estimates a used car's listing price in TRY. Listings are asking prices, so the final sale price can be different.

Damage history is excluded

Reported damage amounts (Tramer) and damage-condition fields are not model inputs because their quality could not be verified. No training rows are removed based on their damage amount.

This estimate does not account for accident history, repairs or damage severity. Two cars with the same entered details receive the same estimate even if their damage histories differ.

Time and coverage

There are no listing dates in the model inputs. These test scores do not prove how well it will predict prices in a future market.

✳

Keep the details honest.

Model selection loads typical specs from the dataset. Check the year, mileage, engine and other details before estimating.

Check damage and repair history separately when comparing real listings.

Local by design

The model runs in your browser. This page does not send the vehicle details you enter to a prediction service.

Predictions are not a vehicle inspection or a market quote.
